translationRepairs: In the seventh year (1827) he was ordered to inspect the Huangjialing dike at Jingshan in northern Huguang and wrote: "Downstream flood victims pleaded urgently for the breached dike to be repaired, while upstream residents claimed the breach outlet led to the old bed of the Xiang River and petitioned again to leave it open.

In the seventh year (1827) he was ordered to inspect the Huangjialing dike at Jingshan in Hubei and wrote: "Downstream flood victims pleaded urgently for the breached dike to be repaired, while upstream residents claimed the breach outlet led to the old bed of the Xiang River and petitioned again to leave it open.
湖北京山 names Jingshan in Hubei; northern Huguang would be 湖廣, so the place correction is required.

In the seventh year he was ordered to inspect the Huangjialing embankment works at Jingshan in northern Huguang and memorialized: 'Downstream disaster victims urgently petitioned to repair the breached dike; upstream residents said the outlet downstream was the old course of the Xiang River and again petitioned to abandon it.

In the seventh year he was ordered to inspect the Huangjialing embankment works at Jingshan in Hubei and memorialized: 'Downstream disaster victims urgently petitioned to repair the breached dike; upstream residents said the outlet downstream was the old course of the Xiang River and again petitioned to abandon it.
The literal field has the same misreading of 湖北 as Huguang; Hubei is the supported province.
He served as subprefect of the Mabian and Fanbian departments and as acting prefect of Zizhou, Meizhou, and Qiongzhou, earning a reputation for sound administration at every post.
He served as subprefect of the Mabian and Guanbian departments and as acting prefect of Zizhou, Meizhou, and Qiongzhou, earning a reputation for sound administration at every post.
瓘邊 is Guanbian; Fanbian would need 番邊, so the hall-name correction is accurate.
He served as subprefect of Mabian and Fanbian departments and as acting prefect of Zizhou, Meizhou, and Qiongzhou, winning a reputation for good government at each post.
He served as subprefect of Mabian and Guanbian departments and as acting prefect of Zizhou, Meizhou, and Qiongzhou, winning a reputation for good government at each post.
The literal field likewise misreads 瓘邊 as Fanbian; Guanbian restores the chapter grapheme.
In the third year (1823) he served as acting governor-general; in the fifth year (1825) he received the full appointment and concurrently acted as regional commander at Chengdu.
In the third year (1823) he served as acting governor-general; in the fifth year (1825) he received the full appointment and concurrently acted as General of Chengdu.
成都將軍 is the Chengdu banner garrison general, not a generic regional commander.
In the third year he acted as governor-general; in the fifth year he received the substantive appointment and concurrently acted as Chengdu regional commander.
In the third year he acted as governor-general; in the fifth year he received the substantive appointment and concurrently acted as Chengdu general.
The literal rendering must likewise keep 成都將軍 as Chengdu general rather than regional commander.

Toudao Stream was the main route by which raw tribesmen entered and left; there too he built an earthen fort manned by military colonists.
頭道溪為生番出入總路 states only that the stream was the raw tribesmen's main route in and out; Han territory is not in the Chinese.

內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat; grand secretary would be 大學士.
After a long while he was promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

The Heng River at Yucheng, Huimin Ditch, the Baqing River at Xiayi, and the flood-relief ditch at Yongcheng had long been the main drainage channels of eastern Henan; repeatedly silted by Yellow River floods, the river districts suffered disaster year after year, and Zuluo had them all dredged.
永城減水溝 is a descriptive flood-relief ditch, not a toponym Jianshui Ditch.

The Heng River at Yucheng, Huimin Ditch, the Baqing River at Xiayi, and the Jianshui Ditch at Yongcheng were formerly key areas in eastern Henan for draining floodwater; repeatedly silted by Yellow River overflows, the river districts suffered disaster year after year—all were dredged.

The literal field likewise turns descriptive 減水溝 into a false proper name.

When the ruffians Zhang Bing, Chen Ban, and others raised a rebellion in Taiwan, General Husong'e was ordered to lead the campaign while Zuluo was charged with rear-area logistics.
瑚松額 must be romanized in full as Husong'e; Husa truncates 松額.

The scoundrels Zhang Bing, Chen Ban, and others in Taiwan raised a rebellion; General Husong'e was ordered to lead troops in suppression, while Zuluo was charged solely with rear-area supplies.

In the thirteenth year (1833) Naval Commander Ma Jisheng defeated the rebels and Zhang Bing was captured; Zuluo went to Taiwan to handle postwar affairs, impeached Colonel Zhou Jinlong and others for ineffective conduct in battle, and stripped or demoted them as appropriate.

In the thirteenth year (1833) Provincial Commander Ma Jisheng defeated the rebels and Zhang Bing was captured; Zuluo went to Taiwan to handle postwar affairs, impeached Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Jinlong and others for ineffective conduct in battle, and stripped or demoted them as appropriate.
提督 is the provincial commander-in-chief, and 都司 is assistant regional commander; naval commander and colonel invent unsupported ranks.

In the thirteenth year Naval Commander Ma Jisheng defeated the bandits and Zhang Bing and others were captured; Zuluo went to Taiwan to arrange postwar affairs, impeached Colonel Zhou Jinlong and others for ineffective offense and defense, and stripped or demoted them according to degree.

In the thirteenth year Provincial Commander Ma Jisheng defeated the bandits and Zhang Bing and others were captured; Zuluo went to Taiwan to arrange postwar affairs, impeached Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Jinlong and others for ineffective offense and defense, and stripped or demoted them according to degree.

提督 is provincial commander, and Zhang Lin's office is the provincial education commissioner (學政); Hanlin examiner is unsupported, while the chapter's 學攻 is the corrupt form of that title.

The dismissed assistant magistrate Qin Shihan memorialized from the capital accusing Naval Commander Ma Jisheng of deceiving the throne to claim merit, and also accusing Zuluo of partiality and deception; Vice Minister Zhao Shengkui and Hanlin examiner Zhang Lin were ordered to investigate; his false charges were cleared and Shihan was banished to Xinjiang.
